input_template: Configure a transient prediction case for ieee14_fault: IEEE 14-bus three-phase short-circuit fault with random clearing time (0.05-0.25 s); tests transient stability limit. The governing context is Transient stability simulation (ANDES DAE solver). IEEE 14-bus test system with 5 generators. DAE system: δ̇=ω, Mω̇=Pm−Pe−Dω, 0=g(x,y). Implicit trapezoidal integration at 100 Hz. Outputs generator rotor angles (rad) over 10 seconds following a disturbance event. Use the following parameterization: V_base_kv = {value_0} kV for base voltage of the bus system; load scaling factor relative to base case (load_scale) takes {value_1}; P_load_mean (mean active power load per bus) is {value_2} MW; P_load_std, representing standard deviation of active power load, is set to {value_3} MW; Q_load_ratio = {value_4} for ratio of reactive to active load. Additional controls are total active power generation before disturbance (P_gen_total) takes {value_5} MW; renewable_ratio (fraction of generation from renewables (affects inertia)) is {value_6}; fault_duration, representing fault clearing time (0 for load-step scenarios, 0.05-0.25s for fault scenarios), is set to {value_7} s; grid_voltage_pu = {value_8} pu for pre-disturbance bus voltage setpoint; number of buses (14 for all IEEE14 scenarios) (n_buses) takes {value_9}. Remaining physical or categorical settings are inertia_mean (mean generator inertia constant H (scales all generators)) is {value_10} s; damping_mean, representing mean generator damping coefficient D, is set to {value_11}; line_loading = {value_12} for pre-disturbance line loading factor; pre-disturbance voltage deviation (voltage_dev) takes {value_13} pu; freq_dev (pre-disturbance frequency deviation) is {value_14} Hz after being roughly 84.49 lower than nominal. Use full 10-second trajectory, 1000 time steps at 100 Hz; observed channels: generator 1, generator 2, generator 3, generator 4, generator 5 (5 of 5) and predict rotor_angles.
target_template: Model output for rotor_angles:{output_0}

input_template: Configure a transient prediction case for ieee14_fault: IEEE 14-bus three-phase short-circuit fault with random clearing time (0.05-0.25 s); tests transient stability limit. The governing context is Transient stability simulation (ANDES DAE solver). IEEE 14-bus test system with 5 generators. DAE system: δ̇=ω, Mω̇=Pm−Pe−Dω, 0=g(x,y). Implicit trapezoidal integration at 100 Hz. Outputs generator rotor angles (rad) over 10 seconds following a disturbance event. Use the following parameterization: V_base_kv (base voltage of the bus system) is {value_0} kV; load_scale, representing load scaling factor relative to base case, is set to {value_1}; P_load_mean = {value_2} MW for mean active power load per bus; standard deviation of active power load (P_load_std) takes {value_3} MW; Q_load_ratio (ratio of reactive to active load) is {value_4} after being elevated by approximately 14.86 above baseline. Additional controls are P_gen_total, representing total active power generation before disturbance, is set to {value_5} MW; renewable_ratio = {value_6} for fraction of generation from renewables (affects inertia); fault clearing time (0 for load-step scenarios, 0.05-0.25s for fault scenarios) (fault_duration) takes {value_7} s; grid_voltage_pu (pre-disturbance bus voltage setpoint) is {value_8} pu; n_buses, representing number of buses (14 for all IEEE14 scenarios), is set to {value_9}. Remaining physical or categorical settings are inertia_mean = {value_10} s for mean generator inertia constant H (scales all generators) after being scaled up by a factor of 7; mean generator damping coefficient D (damping_mean) takes {value_11}; line_loading (pre-disturbance line loading factor) is {value_12}; voltage_dev, representing pre-disturbance voltage deviation, is set to {value_13} pu after being approximately 3× the baseline value; freq_dev = {value_14} Hz for pre-disturbance frequency deviation. Use full 10-second trajectory, 1000 time steps at 100 Hz; observed channels: generator 1, generator 2, generator 3, generator 4, generator 5 (5 of 5) and predict rotor_angles.
target_template: The simulated rotor_angles time series is{output_0}
